summary: Wheeler County, OR lookout in Umatilla NF: tower erected 1931, 40-ft tower 1936, 67-ft tower 1959, last staffed 1974, removed or destroyed 1979; a 1979 survey note reports four concrete leg bases.

facts.design: Successive towers: 50-ft pole or wooden tower with 7x7 cab (1931-32); 40-ft wooden tower with tent cabin (1936); 67-ft treated timber R-6 tower (1959)
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1979 per the two Fire Lookout sources; a 1979 survey note says the tower was torn down and four concrete leg bases remained; no later description found

staffing.status: last staffed 1974; named lookouts listed from 1933 to 1972

events.note: Tree tower erected at Wheeler Point per a Heppner newspaper item dated November 12, 1931; an undated inventory gives a 50-foot pole tower with a 7x7 cab
Firetower.org and firelookout.com date a 40-foot wooden tower and tent cabin to 1936; the Forest Lookouts page dates a 50-foot tower to 1931-32
Forest service plane spotted a one-acre blaze near Lone Rock; a note was dropped to the Wheeler Point lookout and the fire was under control forty minutes later
Bert Mason, Jr., posted at the Wheeler lookout station for the summer
Norbert Peavy stationed as lookout through the 1941 fire season
67-foot treated timber R-6 tower built; the 1959 annual report says the old tower was no longer safe for use
Removed per firetower.org; destroyed per firelookout.com; a 1979 NGS recovery note reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page says the tower was torn down and four concrete leg bases remained
Registered July 18, 2011; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: 15.2 m is 50 feet, the height given for the 1931-32 tower on the Forest Lookouts page. The tower in service from 1959 was 67 feet (20.4 m) per firetower.org. The editor should decide which tower the record describes.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts page gives a 50-foot tower in 1931-32 (Heppner item and undated inventory). Firetower.org and firelookout.com date a 40-foot wooden tower with tent cabin to 1936. The sources do not reconcile, so the story gives both.

Firetower.org says removed in 1979 and firelookout.com says destroyed that year. The 1979 survey note on the Forest Lookouts page says the tower over the station was torn down but also that a new tower had been built west of it. The story reports the note and says the sources do not square.

notes_for_editor: Brief record (elevation 1,522 m, July 18, 2011 registration, gone status) confirmed. Brief height 15.2 m matches the early 50-foot tower; see corrections. Access is not stated in any source, so no access level is recorded. The 1979 NGS note is the latest description found, so today's condition is unknown. Search results mention 1932 and 1959 photos on a Facebook post, but the post was not read and no image URL was captured, so no photo record was added. The 1959 annual report on the Forest Lookouts page has the typo 'Wheedler', which is avoided in quotes.
